title: Run AI at scale with Ray + Kubernetes using Anyscale on Azure | ODSP914

segments.text: KATARINA STANLEY: Welcome
to this session on Anyscale on Azure.
I'm Katarina, a Product Marketing Manager at Anyscale,
and I'm joined today by my colleague Daniel Arrizza,
a Field Engineer here.
Quick agenda.
I'll cover why teams are choosing to own their AI stack,
what makes that hard to scale, and how Anyscale
in Azure addresses it.
Daniel's going to follow with a technical demo,
and we'll close with some next steps.
To jump right in, every team building
with AI today is making a choice on a spectrum.
On one end, you can rent intelligence,
calling someone else's model through an API.
On the other end, you can own it.
And owning is not binary.
It's a spectrum that includes deploying open-source models,
customizing open-source models with your own data,
and training your own models.
Most teams use a mix of both renting and owning.
The question is when ownership makes sense
for a given workload.
So, when is that the case?
It usually comes down to a few things.
Control over your models and your operations,
so you're not exposed to model deprecations,
rate limits or outages.
Data and differentiation, when you need
to keep proprietary data inside your boundary.
And cost and latency, for better unit economics at scale
and faster end-to-end response times.
When one or more of these apply, that's typically
when we see teams move towards ownership.
But here is the challenge point.
Building AI is getting harder because both data
and models are scaling fast.
What used to be structured tabular data is now multimodal.
Data set sizes have moved from gigabytes to petabytes.
Single models are now many models,
and parameter counts are growing exponentially.
Across the AI lifecycle,
that complexity is showing up everywhere.
Building requires coordinated CPU and GPU compute.
Training must be distributed across nodes,
with fault tolerance built in.
And serving requires composing many models,
often on different hardware.
These are problems legacy tools were not designed for.
And teams are increasingly hitting their limits.
It's why we're seeing teams converge on Ray,
the open-source distributed compute framework
for Python and AI workloads.
As AI workloads have grown in scale
and complexity, so has Ray adoption.
It has over 12 million downloads per week
and it's the most widely adopted AI compute framework
across both AI labs and enterprises used by teams
like OpenAI, Uber, TripAdvisor and more.
So, this brings us to Anyscale on Azure from the creators
of Ray and powered by Ray on AKS.
Three core things to know.
First, it accelerates dev to prod with a unified runtime
for multimodal data curation, distributed training
and multimodal online surveying.
Second, it runs reliably at scale
with a fully managed Ray lifecycle on AKS,
a priority aware scheduler that maximizes GPU utilization
and 24/7 Ray expert support.
And third, it's Azure native.
It runs on AKS in your own subscription,
integrates with Entra ID for RBAC and is available
through the Azure portal.
So, your data and IP stay inside your existing security
and governance boundaries.
So, with that, I'm going to hand it over to Daniel to walk you
through what building, training and serving on Anyscale
in Azure looks like in practice.
